incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2026-04-09T11:42Z -> runtime-pool/prod-usw - symptom summary: gradual GPU memory creep in paged-attention + kv-cache leading to OOM exit (SIGKILL) and node Recreate events in us-west-2a. Detected 11:35Z. Severity=P1.
Alex: I'm oncall. Drop quick scope and impact.
Priya: observed progressive kv_page_count increase across 4 pods in runtime-paid-usw-2. Error timeline shows first allocation failure at 11:34:12Z, multiple container kills after that. Affected tenant: orchid-ads heavy carousel generation. 5xxs + latency spikes for that tenant only.
Ravi: grabbed logs from pod runtime-paid-84c9f: 
```
[2026-04-09T11:34:11Z] DEBUG paged: request(ctx=orchid-ads/job=9876) reserve_pages=128
[2026-04-09T11:34:12Z] WARN paged_alloc: cannot_reserve pages=128 free=8
[2026-04-09T11:34:12Z] ERROR cuda: cuMemAlloc_v2 failed: out of memory (no memory left on device)
[2026-04-09T11:34:12Z] ERROR runtime: fatal: GPU OOM - killing worker
[2026-04-09T11:34:13Z] INFO kube: ContainerExited status=137
```
Maya: nvidia-smi on host gpu-07 shows a single process consuming ~39800MiB on 40GB card. Process claim doesn't drop on container exit until kubelet reaps it.
Jordan: runbook suggests two fast mitigations: 1) tenant token-bucket throttle via admin API; 2) disable attention paging for the specific model variant on the tenant.
runbook-bot: PAGED-ALLOC-ESCALATE runbook -> quick steps:
  - query `/metrics/kv_usage` to pick top offenders
  - run `redwood admin tenant throttle <tenant> --ratio 0.2` to shed load
  - toggle model paging: `redwood admin model set-flag --model lm-carousel-v1 --flag paged_attention=false --tenant orchid-ads`
  - if pods still crash, cordon node and restart kubelet to release NVML handles; as last resort reboot node.
Alex: enforcing throttle now, applying model flag next.
```
$ redwood admin tenant throttle orchid-ads --ratio 0.15 --reason "OOM mitigation"
Applied throttle: orchid-ads -> 15% of previous ingest rate
$ redwood admin model set-flag --model lm-carousel-v1 --flag paged_attention=false --tenant orchid-ads
Flag applied: paged_attention=false for tenant orchid-ads
```
Ravi: kicking off kv eviction on the worst pod: 
```
$ kubectl exec -n runtime runtime-paid-84c9f -c runtime -- /usr/local/bin/kv-tool shrink --target-pages=2000 --burst=1500
started eviction: before=14200 after=~11800 (initial)
```
Priya: after 8 minutes: per-pod kv pages down ~55%, GPU mem on worst node down to 22GB, pod restarts drop from 6->1 in last 10 minutes. Orchid-ads 5xx rate fell to baseline. However one node still shows high hold due to leaked NVML handles.
Maya: I see node event `NodeRecreate` on gpu-07 with kube-proxy restart; apparently the CRI didn't reap container process promptly. I'm cordoning gpu-07 for remediation.
Alex: cordon+drain gpu-07, then restart kubelet and NV driver.
Jordan: sequence executed: 
```
$ kubectl cordon gpu-07
$ kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
$ ssh gpu-07 "sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker"
$ ssh gpu-07 "sudo /sbin/reboot"  # if handles persist
```
Note: we prefer restart kubelet & nvidia services first to avoid full node reboot when possible.
Maya: post-restart `nvidia-smi` clean. Pods rescheduled to healthy nodes. System-level leak appears cleared.
Ravi: dug into heap traces; found repeated small-page allocs that never decrement refcount due to race between async refill and eviction path. Snapshot: 
```
kv_inc_ref(page=0x12cfa, prev=1 -> now=2)  # ref bumped by refill thread
evict_check: page=0x12cfa ref=2 skip
refdec from consumer path missed due to early abort on signal -> no decrement
```
This yields slow accumulation of pages that can't be evicted until refcount threshold is dropped.
Alex: propose short-term: lower eviction-skip threshold and add aggressive periodic scavenger that forcefully decays stale refs after X minutes. Plan a code patch for allocator.
runbook-bot: SUGGESTED HOTFIX: set env REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_REF_THRESHOLD=1 and REDWOOD_KV_SCAVENGE_INTERVAL=60s on canary.
Jordan: deployed canary change on 2 pods in us-west-2b with those env vars. Observing for 6h.
Priya: monitoring: canary pods show kv page churn down and no sustained growth during 1h. CPU marginally up on allocator sweeps. No customer-visible regressions.
Maya: CS update: orchid-ads contacted, we informed them of temporary throttle and config toggles. Two support tickets (SUP-1981, SUP-1982) opened; CS will send follow-up and RCA when postmortem ready.
Alex: handoff time ~13:05Z. Summary for next oncall (Talia): cause: paged-attention allocator refcount race -> slow kv accumulation -> GPU OOM -> container restarts. Scope: 4 pods on 2 nodes, single tenant orchid-ads impacted. Actions taken: tenant throttle (15%), model paging disabled for tenant, kv eviction, cordon+restart node, canary allocator scavenger env set. Current status: stable, on monitoring.
Talia: taking over. Follow-ups:
- Ravi: open PR for allocator refcount decay & add unit tests (due EOD)
- Priya: add alert for `kv_page_growth_rate > 1000/min` and `nvml_handle_count>0 after container exit` (due tomorrow)
- Jordan: prepare rollout playbook for full defrag rollout (runbook update) (due next week)
- Maya: coordinate customer comms and check for any billing implications (due tomorrow)
Alex: handing over. Leaving traces and full logs in incident ticket INC-7402. Ping me if escalates. :thumbsup:
runbook-bot: Incident 2026-04-09T11:42Z status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff complete to Talia at 13:05Z.
Talia: acknowledging, monitoring for 6h, will escalate if growth resumes.
